title: Auth Control Plane refresh exchange response (v2 wire format, asymmetric access token)
description: A successful refresh when the access token is the EdDSA access-token.v1 JWS (CHAOS-10450), with the ROTATED opaque refresh credential. v1 stays the surface of the HS256 token; v2 is the new surface version refresh-response.v1 names for an asymmetric token. Both coexist until the HS256 issuer is removed. v2 carries two tokens of one session: access_token for go-api and query-api, session_access_token for auth-service's session routes (an EdDSA user token carries one audience). Rotation is single use with a 30 s concurrent-refresh grace (the grace answer returns the same successor). The old user object is not part of this contract; clients read session.v1.

schema_version.description: Contract identifier. A reader MUST reject an unrecognised value (G-26: unknown denies); additive evolution stays in v2 (TRD section 21).

access_token.description: Compact JWS of an access-token.v1 user access token. A schema cannot decode a segment, so the shape is all it states: three non-empty base64url segments of a possible length (a segment of 4k+1 characters is no base64url). ParseRefreshResponse decodes every segment strictly (no padding, no non-zero trailing bits). ParseRefreshResponse then decodes the header and the payload and runs them through ParseAccessToken (alg EdDSA, typ at+jwt, kid, closed header and claims, no duplicate member, lifetime ceiling), refuses a token whose audience is not dev-health-api (scope api:access, the token go-api and query-api accept) or whose sid is not session_id, and refuses an expires_in that is not exp - iat. The signature is not checked here: a reader that acts on the token verifies it against jwks.v1 first.

expires_in.description: Access token lifetime in seconds, exp - iat of the token: 1 to 3600 (the access-token.v1 ceiling, AccessTokenLifetimeCeiling). Integer token only; 600.0 passes the schema and both clients refuse it.

refresh_credential.description: Opaque refresh credential: URL-safe base64 characters only, 43-256 long. A dot is not in the alphabet, so a refresh JWT cannot be presented here. A SECRET: it exists on the wire only in the refresh request and the refresh response, never in session.v1 or auth-outcome.v1, never in a log, metric label or audit row.

refresh_expires_in.description: Rotated refresh credential lifetime in seconds; the 7 day ceiling is today's RefreshLifetime.

session_access_token.description: Compact JWS of the access-token.v1 user access token of audience auth-service (scope auth:session): the one auth-service's session routes accept (GET /v1/sessions/current, the revoke routes, the social link routes, change-password). The same session, key and lifetime as access_token, its own jti. ParseRefreshResponse applies the access_token rules to it (strict segments, ParseAccessToken), refuses an audience other than auth-service, a sid that is not session_id, and a lifetime that is not expires_in. A v1 answer has no such member: the session routes accept the HS256 token itself. The signature is not checked here.

session_id.description: Opaque server-minted session identifier. An identifier, never a secret, and never copied from caller input.
